reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check the refunds table against the batch's requested refunds, since the handoff message alone isn't verification.
The refunds table matches the batch's requested refunds exactly (orders 102, 103, 105 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the orders to identify the customers to pay.
The refunds table matches the batch exactly, so I can proceed. The customers in the orders are acme, birch, and cobalt, and I'll get each net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 33983. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme and birch balances are in hand. Cobalt is the last customer in the orders, so I need its net balance before recording any payouts.
All three customers now have net balances, and the refunds table matched the batch exactly. I'll record acme's payout of 33983 first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's balance of 65068 matches its orders (29562 + 35506) with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch payouts are recorded. The refunds matched the batch exactly, and cobalt's net balance of 2634 comes from net_balance, so I'll record that payout now.

All three payouts were recorded and each matches a manual check: acme 27247+18968-12232=33983, birch 29562+35506=65068, cobalt 4653+33845-2289-33575=2634. The refunds table matched the batch exactly, so the batch is complete.
